title: Closed-system automated microdistillation of small-volume water samples for tritium and stable isotope analysis
author: Butera, Wassenaar, et al.

steps.title: Inspect components and add beads
steps.instruction: Check all EvapoClean parts (distillation vial, collection vial, caps, fluoropolymer elbow) for cleanliness, dryness, and damage; verify numbered vials match caps; place three clean glass boiling beads into each distillation vial.

steps.title: Weigh components with caps
steps.instruction: Install caps on each vial, weigh each assembled component, and record the mass; this pre‑weighing will be used for post‑distillation recovery calculations.

steps.title: Load sample and optional neutralizer
steps.instruction: Add water by mass (e.g., 12.0 g, up to a maximum of 20.0 g) to the pre‑weighed distillation vial containing the beads and record the final pre‑distillation mass. For samples requiring neutralization, weigh 4 g of PbCl₂ in a disposable vial and add it to the same distillation vial after the water sample.

steps.title: Cap distillation vial
steps.instruction: Immediately and firmly cap the distillation vial to prevent evaporation while preparing the remaining samples.

steps.title: Assemble closed‑system vessel
steps.instruction: When ready to distill, uncapped the distillation vial, hold it vertically to avoid spillage, screw it into the fluoropolymer elbow, then attach the collection vial to close the system. Tighten both vial‑to‑elbow connections firmly but without overtightening (to avoid thread stripping or deformation) and keep the distillation vial upright to prevent cross‑contamination.

steps.title: Perform microdistillation
steps.instruction: Place the assembled vessels (up to twelve 25 mL kits) into the heating block set to either 100 °C or 155 °C and run the automated microdistillation as per the instrument’s program (duration not specified in the source).

steps.title: Cap vessels after distillation
steps.instruction: Immediately after the heating cycle, cap both the distillation and collection vials to minimize evaporative loss.

steps.title: Post‑distillation weighing (optional)
steps.instruction: Weigh the capped distillation vial (and optionally the collection vial) to determine gravimetric recovery, comparing to the pre‑distillation mass recorded earlier.

steps.title: Prepare liquid scintillation sample
steps.instruction: Mix 8 mL of the distilled water sample with 12 mL of Ultima Gold scintillation cocktail, place the mixture in a counting vial, and count for 500 minutes using a HIDEX Ultra‑Low‑Level Analyzer (ULLA).

description: Validation experiments were designed to independently assess water recovery, salt removal, isotopic integrity, and memory effects under worst-case salinity, alkalinity, and isotopic enrichment conditions. Stable isotope (δ2H, δ18O) compositions of pre- and post-distilled samples were measured in the Jan Veizer Stable Isotope Laboratory at the University of Ottawa by laser spectroscopy. The natural abundance samples were analyzed on a Picarro water isotope analyzer (L2130-i), whereas the deuterium-enriched samples were analyzed using the Liquid Water Isotope Water Analyzer (LIWA-45EP) by Los Gatos Research (LGR) [13]. All results are reported on the VSMOW scale. Tritium measurements were performed in the André E. Lalonde National Facility for Accelerator Mass Spectrometry (AEL-AMS) by liquid scintillation counting (LSC) using a HIDEX Ultra-Low-Level Analyzer (ULLA). Tritium activities (reported in Bq L⁻¹) of distilled test water samples were determined using established techniques (8 mL distilled water sample + 12 mL Ultima Gold scintillation cocktail) using a 500-minute counting time. •Quantitative recovery of water was achieved during automated microdistillation, with gravimetric recoveries ranging from 99.7 % to 99.9 % across all 12 purification ports (Table 1).•Distillation reduced the electrical conductivity of a wide range of saline and alkaline samples to levels compatible with downstream liquid scintillation counting and stable isotope analysis for all tested water sample matrices, including sodium chloride and sea-salt solutions (Tables 3 and 5).Table 3Electrical conductivity (µS cm⁻¹) of NaCl solutions before and after microdistillation in the EvapoClean system.Table 3 dummy alt textVial #[NaCl] (g L⁻¹)Electrical Conductivity (pre)Electrical Conductivity (post)1100127,47552100127,47523100127,475347095,875257095,875267095,875273554,1373083554,1372093554,13737101525,62537111525,6252121525,625315894822589482•Hydrogen and oxygen isotope ratios (δ²H and δ¹⁸O) me
